column1: # 1A.1 resolution ledger: the stepping-stone merge (PLAN.md r46a §6.1 row 1A.1), one row per conflict hunk.
# Branch stone-1a, cut from origin/main 6c7401ce0; merge of upstream 74d0c72fd; merge base ba398dfff3e3.
# Step 1 left 381 conflict hunks in 81 content files (16,263 conflict lines) and 121 modify/delete paths.
# Rows after the 381 hunk rows: edits outside the conflict regions that a resolution required (hunk
# "clean:<what>", same commit), and the follow-up fix commits (group R1A, hunk "fix:<what>").
#   group    the file group that resolved it (g01..g11, R1A's nested workers; R1A for follow-up fixes)
#   commit   the commit that holds the resolution (the merge commit, or a follow-up fix commit)
#   hunk     n/N in the conflicted file (the order of its <<<<<<< blocks), or a name for a non-hunk row
#   line     the first line inside the <<<<<<< block in the conflicted file (- for a non-hunk row)
#   class    the ownership class (§2.1, tools/classify_owner.py): 1 policy seams, 2 Windows platform,
#            3 terminal core, 4 libghostty-vt C API, 5 other shared core, 6 shell integration,
#   side     fork | upstream | both (both sides' lines) | hand (a rewritten combination) | neither
#   rule     what decided it (§2.1 default side, §2.2.4 ancestry clause, §2.3 exception, §2.4 page model, ...)
#   commits  the upstream and fork commits that decided it (short SHAs)
#   entries  the Self-Correction Log entries that govern it (<area file>:<date> <subject>), or -
#   lead     -, or the lead's decision that governs the row (LEAD <id> <date>: ...); no row is provisional
# Per-hunk view of what each resolution dropped: git show --remerge-diff <merge commit>.
